title: ChIRP-Seq
scope: Illumina explanatory ChIRP schematic, specifically the RNA-directed chromatin capture to genomic-DNA readout path supported by Chu et al. (PMID 21963238). ChIRP is the capture method and ChIRP-seq its sequencing readout; the card uses the names interchangeably. The image ends at extracted DNA; broad library construction and sequencing/genomic localization are explicitly marked text-supported extensions. The related dChIRP publication (PMID 24997788) establishes a distinct domain-level variant only at abstract level; its implementation is not assigned the depicted operations. Protein/RNA assay branches from the primary paper, early morpholino optimization and catalogue kit names are not depicted workflows and are not added. No origin/priority or equivalence to other capture methods is asserted.

states.label: Chromatin associated with target ncRNA and RNA-binding protein
features: Purple ncRNA and blue RNA-binding protein are shown over a black chromatin DNA line flanked by grey nucleosome-like bodies.

The far-left title vignette repeats the input arrangement and contains a short yellow DNA highlight. No legend defines that highlight, and no arrow connects the two left-hand drawings as separate transformations.
The target ncRNA supplies the capture identity; genomic DNA associated with that RNA is the eventual sequenced analyte.

operations.label: Crosslink / Fragment
operations.description: Stabilize the ncRNA-protein-chromatin associations and fragment the chromatin preparation. The continuous chromatin input becomes shorter pieces while a target-associated RNA/protein/DNA assembly remains recoverable. The card identifies sonication as the fragmentation operation.
operations.mechanism: Crosslinking retains associations present in cells; sonication solubilizes and fragments chromatin and can also shear the RNA.
operations.information_effect: The retained association between selected RNA and genomic DNA is carried forward in fragmented complexes; the drawing does not encode a particular crosslinker.

operations.label: RNase H
operations.description: The depicted bead-attached assembly loses its RNA/probe/bead connection and yields a protein-associated DNA fragment. For the cited Chu et al. implementation, interpret this as RNase A plus RNase H elution, explicitly resolving the schematic RNase H-only label.
operations.mechanism: RNA-directed nuclease elution disrupts the RNA bridge and preferentially releases RNA-associated chromatin from the capture support. The RNases are treatment reagents, not readout products.
operations.information_effect: Physical RNA linkage is disrupted after it has selected the DNA. The recovered DNA retains the genomic localization information; preferential RNA-bridge release does not establish absolute exclusion of off-target DNA.

corrections.diagram_observation: The arrow after streptavidin bead capture is labeled RNase H; its product is a blue protein on a short black DNA line, with the purple RNA and bead no longer drawn. The card also mentions RNase H alone.
corrections.primary_statement: The inspected primary paper reports RNase A plus RNase H for DNA elution and explains that this preferentially releases DNA recovered through an RNA bridge rather than direct probe-DNA binding. The operation and released-material state explicitly use that primary implementation while preserving the source label.

evidence.locator: RNase H arrow: bead/probe/purple RNA assembly becomes a blue protein on a short black DNA line

evidence.quote: In this method, samples are first crosslinked and sonicated. Biotinylated tiling oligos are hybridized to the RNAs of interest, and the complexes are captured with streptavidin magnetic beads. After treatment with RNase H, the DNA is extracted and sequenced.

evidence.locator: [b00012], Results: RNA-bridged DNA elution
evidence.quote: We gently eluted DNA off of beads using a combination of RNase A and RNase H so that only DNA retrieved via a RNA bridge, but not direct probe-DNA interaction, could be preferentially released.
